sections.heading: C — Weather and trip planning
sections.markdown:
## C — Weather and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A108
Before a trip, consider whether travel is necessary and whether a shared ride or public transportation can meet the need. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A108
Using available public transport or carpools can reduce personal driving. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A108
Avoiding peak traffic can reduce wear and strain on the driver and vehicle. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A108
Combine errands by listing needed items and destinations and visiting several places during one trip. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A108
Call ahead to confirm that needed items or pickups are ready before driving. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A108
Trip planning that reduces unnecessary travel can save time and cost and reduce road traffic. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A108
Before travel, check windows, lights, tires, fluid levels, belts, hoses and brakes. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A108
Get adequate sleep the night before beginning a trip. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A108
Plan departure time to avoid urban congestion where possible. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A108
Prepare route, entrance and exit numbers and account for rest, fuel, meal and construction stops. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A108
Carry a highlighted map or written route description as a travel reference. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A108
The handbook's major-highway planning estimate is about 100 to 110 miles in two hours, with slower progress on secondary roads, through towns or in mountains. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A108
For trip planning, the handbook recommends 10-to-15-minute breaks every two to three hours and about an hour for meals. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A108
For one person doing all the driving, the handbook recommends considering a six-to-eight-hour driving day the limit. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A108
When drivers share duties, the handbook recommends no more than about 10 to 11 total driving hours in a day. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A108
Avoid night travel when visibility is poor, particularly after 11 p.m. when falling asleep is more likely. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A108
Pack spare keys in case the primary set is lost or locked inside. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A108
Carry insurance details, money for planned and unexpected costs, the vehicle manual and local maps. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0108]

Misconceptions: Daily trip-duration guidance is not a statutory driving-hours limit; good winter tires do not remove other traffic and visibility risks; a hot tire's increased pressure is not a reason to bleed it; severe-weather shelter advice has explicit unresolved conditions.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: plan, inspect, equip, reassess. It organizes preparation without adding weather thresholds or escape instructions.
Glossary: Distinguish trip-planning estimate, survival kit, freeze-resistant washer fluid, coolant warning, bleeding tar and severe-weather source debt using the fact blocks.
Dynamic facts: Conditions change during a trip. Equipment recommendations depend on the vehicle manual; edition-bound tire dates and emergency procedures require issuer refresh. No current weather forecast or unverified rescue technique is asserted.
